questions: Did these movements begin suddenly, over minutes to hours?
Did they begin after a recent stroke, head injury, or other neurological illness?
Did you recently start, stop, or change the dose of any medication?
Have you taken any antipsychotic, nausea medication such as metoclopramide or prochlorperazine, or Parkinson medication?
Are the movements present continuously while you are awake?
Do the movements stop completely when you are asleep?
Can you voluntarily stop the movements for a few seconds?
Do you feel an uncomfortable urge or inner restlessness before making the movements?
Do the movements lessen when you concentrate on another task?
Do they become worse when you voluntarily move the affected hand?
Have you had weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, facial drooping, or loss of vision?
Have you ever had similar movements involving the face, tongue, other arm, or legs?
Have you had episodes of staring, loss of awareness, confusion, or memory gaps with these movements?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, lupus, or another autoimmune disease?
Have you had fever, weight loss, cancer, or a recent infection?
Has anyone in your family had involuntary movements, Huntington disease, or a similar neurological condition?
Have you previously had Parkinson disease or another movement disorder?
Do the movements cause pain or injury to your hand or arm?
